messages:
Noah: Quick sync — picking up the follow-up for the controlplane onboarding RFC. We still need to pick between the ephemeral-shim pattern (agent + short-lived TLS to CP) vs permanent per-tenant peering for new enterprise onboards. Thoughts?
Maria: TL;DR: shim = faster ops, less infra cost, more transient connections. Peering = stable routing, preserves source IPs, but higher network/account complexity.
Devon: From infra perspective: peering gives predictable network path and avoids NAT hairpins. But peering scale = more VPC attachments and routing tables to manage.
Sam: Security note: shim forces us to terminate mTLS in our control plane unless agent proxies end-to-end. That increases blast radius if CP creds leak.
Olivia: We could implement a shim that forwards encrypted customer traffic (L4 passthrough) and only uses TLS for control messages. That mitigates termination risk.
Noah: Good. Want concrete tradeoffs: latency, ops, cost, cert rotation, troubleshooting. Can we summarize in a mini decision table?
Ben: Short bullets:
- Latency: peering ~ low jitter. shim depends on relay hop but often negligible if regional relays.
- Cost: peering upfront config + cross-account ops; shim = bandwidth + relay infra.
- Troubleshooting: peering = customer network team involved; shim = our logs but easier SRE blameless postmortem.
Clara: Also think about long tail: When customers want static egress IPs preserved for allowlist, peering shines. Shim requires NAT preservation hacks or an egress-preserving relay.
Devon: Implementation effort: peering flow: set up peering + route propagation + ACL testing. Shim flow: ship agent, open outbound to relay, register. Agent lifecycle easier to automate.
Maria: Operation mode idea: offer shim as default for self-serve onboarding and peering as opt-in enterprise add-on. That splits cost/ops.
Sam: +1 but we need a clear failure mode for shim: relay outage must fallback to alternative region or dedicated footprint. Avoid cascading CP overload.
Noah: Agreed. What's the minimal pilot? I propose: 1) implement L4-forwarding shim (no CP TLS termination) 2) add egress-preserve option (NAT-preserve) for customers who need source IPs 3) pilot with two non-critical enterprise customers and measure latency/ops.
Olivia: For NAT-preserve, we can add path to route via a small regional egress fleet that performs SNAT from per-customer pool. Will need IP lease manager.
Ben: IP lease manager = new stateful component. Ops cost non-trivial but scoped. Could reuse existing egress-operator code.
Clara: Certificate rotation: shim agent only needs mTLS certs for auth to controlplane; if L4 passthrough we don't touch customer certs. So rotation surface smaller. Still need short TTL certs for agents.
Devon: Suggest agent keepalive and reconnect backoff defaults: 30s keepalive, exponential backoff to 5m cap. Also surface metrics: connection duration, reconnect rate, bytes forwarded.
Noah: Can someone draft the follow-up RFC with these bullets + migration/playbook? I can own the pilot coordination.
Maria: I can draft the RFC. Will include config snippet for agent: ```
agent:
  mode: shim
  forward_mode: l4-passthrough
  keepalive: 30s
  nat_preserve: optional
  cert_ttl: 24h
```
Sam: Add a troubleshooting checklist: how to capture packet path, relay health, and fallback test commands (curl via agent, tcpdump on relay).
Olivia: Also add an ops rollback: switch registered agent to fail-open->direct-peer mode if pilot needs lift-and-shift.
infra-bot: Deploy pipeline note: make sure we gate relay scaling autoscaler behind canary for pilot customers.
Ben: Next steps: Maria to open RFC PR by EOW; Noah to contact two pilot customers; Dev to stub IP lease manager spike; Sam to write fallback checklist.
Noah: Perfect. If RFC PR lands today we can schedule a 30m sync Thurs to finalize SLOs. :thumbsup:
